claim: Let \(N\ge2\), let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N\) be a bounded domain containing the origin, put \(R_\Omega=\sup_{x\in\Omega}|x|\), \(X_1(r)=(\log(e/r))^{-1}\), \(X_2=X_1\circ X_1\), \(N' = N/(N-1)\), and fix \(\beta>1\). Define \(w_\beta=X_1(|x|/R_\Omega)^{-\beta(N-1)}\), \(a=(\beta-1)/N'\), and the weighted Hardy defect \[I_{\beta,\Omega}[u]=\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^Nw_\beta\,dx-a^N\int_\Omega \frac{|u|^N}{|x|^N}X_1(|x|/R_\Omega)^{N-(N-1)\beta}\,dx.\] For every real \(q<2\), \[\inf_{0\ne u\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\setminus\{0\})}\frac{I_{\beta,\Omega}[u]}{\int_\Omega \frac{|u|^N}{|x|^N}X_1^{N-(N-1)\beta}X_2^q\,dx}=0.\] Consequently the exponent \(1/(N-1)\) of \(X_2\) in Theorem 1.4 of arXiv:2610.03668v1 is optimal also for \(\beta>1\): if \(\theta<1/(N-1)\) and \(\alpha>0\), then \[\sup_{I_{\beta,\Omega}[u]\le1}\int_\Omega \exp\!\left(\alpha |u|^{N'}X_1^{-\beta}X_2^{\theta}\right)\,dx=\infty.\] Thus the source theorem’s positive \(\beta>1\) embedding has the same sharp logarithmic correction exponent as its \(\beta<1\) regime.
integrity: The proof independently derives the missing \(\beta>1\) subquadratic-remainder obstruction and uses only the focal paper’s published Hardy inequality and its parameter-independent Young factorization. Search non-detection is not treated as proof of priority.
scientific_limitations: The theorem proves failure of every \(X_2^q\) Hardy remainder with \(q<2\); it does not prove existence or a best constant at \(q=2\) for \(\beta>1\).
The Leray–Trudinger consequence determines the correction exponent, not the largest admissible exponential coefficient \(\alpha\).
The focal preprint is very recent, so indexing lag or an equivalent argument under different terminology remains a residual originality risk.
No independent audit has been performed.
title: The sharp \(X_2\) exponent persists for \(\beta>1\) in the log-weighted Leray–Trudinger inequality
